entityDescription:
The satellite market is booming, with projections of over 60,000 orbiting objects by 2030. However, strong sustainability challenges arise as satellites have a short lifespan, resulting in overcrowded orbits and $1 trillion worth of value loss due to inoperative assets. In-Orbit Services (IOS) like refueling, repairing, and life extension are proven to be the solution for the expanding satellite population. However, current IOS prototypes face hurdles due to limited autonomy and tailored mission focus, resulting in a lack of scalability and economic inefficiency. A shift towards multi-mission capabilities is crucial to forming a self-sustained space ecosystem, enabling cost reductions and wider market access.

SPAICE pioneered leveraging Generative AI and Deep Reinforcement Learning to develop the first fully autonomous solution to enable In-Orbit Services at scale. Our proprietary software tools enable autonomous navigation and multitasking robotic services and integrate with existing satellites to improve their capabilities. Our software is delivered through a plug-and-play servicing platform including sensors, robot arms, and a computing unit. As a modular payload, our platform is ready to be integrated into any existing satellite, transforming it into a functional in-orbit servicer. Spaice is the first universal AI-based solution for space services, agnostic to any target satellite and capable of performing several robotic operations.

Our primary clients are satellite manufacturers, as our focus involves integrating our robotic platform with their satellite buses to convert them into servicers. We sell them our robotic kit and software charged as a one-time license. These servicers will be used to provide services to constellation operators, for which we will charge a periodic fee. Providers of IOS missions represent an additional sales stream. These companies currently perform in-orbit rendezvous and docking demonstrations with individual targets and aim to scale their services to multiple missions. Our multitask kit is the perfect solution to enable their scalability.

entityDescription:
The ECGS was created in Luxembourg on June 13th, 1988 (as published in the Memorial “C” N.41- February 15, 1989, pp 1936-1938) in accord with the Accord Partiel Ouvert (APO) established by Governments from the States Member of the European Council.
This APO, concerning prevention, protection and assistance organization against technological and major natural risks (Agreement EUR-OPA on Major Risks) has passed the Resolution (87) 2 from the 2ndof March 1987, in which European Community Commission and the UNESCO, the Health World Organization and the Humanitary Affairs Department from the United Nations took part.
On May 17th, 1994, a Convention was signed in-between ECGS and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, defining the following tasks for which the ECGS will be supported:
- To promote programs in Geodynamics Research, related to the study of Tectonics Distortions in connection with Earthquakes,with a particular emphasize on Space Techniques.
- To improve the relationship between specialists from different scientific disciplines by supporting regular meetings as part of the Journées Luxembourgeoises de Géodynamique (JLG), and also by encouraging colloquia and workshops.
- To equip the Underground Geodynamics Laboratory in Walferdange with the necessary scientific and technical equipment for the study of deformation in a tectonically active zone, in order to test its performance in an aseismic site.
- To undertake these specific actions in a scientific interest.
The Grand Duchy of Luxembourgprovides annual support to:
- Cover the cost of the permanent staff
- Organize the Journées Luxembourgeoises de Geodynamique (JLG)
- Colloquia and workshops related to geodynamics and seismology
- Support will also be provided to cover the cost of publishing the “Cahiers de l’ECGS” and
- the cost of the maintenance and equipment of the Walferdange Geodynamic Laboratory.

• In-orbit configurability and update capability

entityDescription: ADAPTA Studio is a spinoff of Politecnico di Milano that has made 3D accessible to everyone through the development of algorithms for the optimization and management of models, spaces, and scans, patented and usable through a Cloud service. ADAPTA has designed a cloud service, "AMAZ3D," to democratize the use and distribution of 3D models, spaces, and scans (hereinafter referred to as 3D assets) to meet the growing demand for digital content. In fact, one of the main challenges in the field of 3D applications (Gaming, CAD, Digital Twin, Training, etc.) today is to have real-time interactions with the highest possible graphical performance. ADAPTA has developed innovative algorithms that significantly reduce the polygon count and weight of 3D assets while maintaining the quality and final graphical performance as much as possible, making it usable on any type of device (PC, smartphone, tablet, headsets, etc.) with a focus on digital multichannel for the end user (Web, Mobile, Augmented and Virtual Reality) with optimal performance. Furthermore, AMAZ3D not only optimizes the 3D model but also manages the entire document flow (storage, versioning, sharing, etc.) through a repository and a 3D viewer integrable into apps and third-party systems. The company is currently evolving AMAZ3D to also support next-generation 3D tools for the automatic reconstruction of three-dimensional assets based on artificial intelligence techniques such as NERF/Gaussian Splatting.

Pileus Scandinavia, further in the text called Pileus, is a newly started company that aims to bring new technology from Luleå University of Technology, regarding ice detection and forecast for ice formation on wind turbines, to the market.
The technology has been validated during two winter seasons together with Vattenfall and Statkraft and has proven to be superior to other technology available today. Pileus technology is able to detect 97% of cases, which can be compared to today's system that can handle 2%.
Being able to detect with very high accuracy and accuracy when ice begins to accumulate on wind turbines and being able to provide a forecast of what the risk looks like for the next 24 hours provides very great benefits for wind power producers. The advantages concern both electricity production, security and pricing linked to the common electricity market, Nord Pool. Energy losses due to ice and snow can amount to 10-15% of total production during a winter, i.e. large energy loss and reduced revenues for owners of wind farms.
By using Pileus technology, this figure can be greatly reduced and electricity production optimized by using our forecast for weather and icing.
